bounds.domain: One mounted hook, two native port identities, two replacements including A to B to A, one teardown, two reads, and up to two serial sign-out calls. Reads and sign-out calls can settle after their port or revision changes.
bounds.assumptions: Port operations return an opaque verified snapshot, refusal, or cancellation. A host can reject an aborted read with a regular error. The read publication and sign-out reset run synchronously after their ownership checks. Host reply fairness is optional and does not require success.
bounds.limitations: Models renderer account and availability publication for a supplied session port. Omits the legacy web/remote backend, explicit activation and event routing, native credential storage, periodic poll timing, and provider error payloads. Mounted conformance controls the native port and runs the production hook. It is scenario conformance and does not replay generated model traces.

assumptions: Weak fairness of each pending read reply and the active sign-out reply. Aborting a host signal fences publication but does not guarantee that the host promise returns.
No fairness. A controlled host can keep a read or sign-out pending indefinitely, even after the renderer has retired the revision.
No fairness. Before the fix, an aborted port can reject with a regular error and publish unavailable after the captured revision is retired.
